catalyst: Question 8 repeal of adult-use sales failed by about 3 to 1 on Nov 3 (over 80% counted). Next: the CCC’s Oct 22 draft medical rules would end mandatory vertical integration (new standalone medical dispensary license; 36-month transition for existing treatment centers) and drop patient residency
ib_angle: Repeal overhang removed for ~800 licensed businesses; standalone medical licenses would add doors and let treatment centers drop cultivation or manufacturing.
source: NORML (Nov 4 results); The Marijuana Herald (CCC Oct 22 materials)

catalyst: Democrats won the Senate majority on Nov 3 (flipping four GOP seats, losing one) while keeping the House and governor (Shapiro reelected), the first Democratic trifecta in decades; adult-use 'may be on the table in 2027'. House passed HB 1200 in 2025. Next vehicle is the FY27-28 budget
ib_angle: Medical-only with capped permits keeps doors scarce (Cresco paid $50M for 9 stores). A Democratic trifecta raises 2027 adult-use odds, which would re-rate incumbents.

catalyst: Adult-use retail sales start Jul 1, 2027. CCA released draft regulations Sep 2026 (final expected December); license applications open Feb 1, 2027 and initial licenses are due by May 1, 2027; 350-store cap; 6% state tax (8% after Jul 2029)
ib_angle: Greenfield build-out: applicants need capital and operating partners; existing vertical medical operators are best placed to convert.
source: Virginia Cannabis Control Authority; Virginia Business (draft regs, Sep 11)

catalyst: DOH final order (Sep 11) issued all 22 new vertically integrated MMTC licenses from the 2023 round; denied applicants had 30 days to seek review at the 1st DCA. Each licensee had to post a $5M bond by Sep 25 and must request cultivation, processing and dispensing authorization within 180, 270 and 365 days. Adult-use ballot dismissed — next attempt 2028
ib_angle: 22 new licensees funding build-outs → financing, JV and sale mandates; incumbents are consolidating (Vireo closed FLUENT's 33 stores Nov 9; Planet 13 holder vote Dec 10).

catalyst: SB 56 (eff. Mar 20): 400-dispensary statewide cap (~200 open), 8-store per-operator limit, 1-mile spacing between stores, 70% THC cap on extracts
ib_angle: Capped adult-use market with room to grow; distressed exits (Cannabist→Holistic $47M, AYR→Arboretum) and Vireo's 4-deal vertical entry.

catalyst: Democrats won the governor's race (Hinojosa) and lieutenant governor (Vikki Goodwin unseated Dan Patrick) on Nov 3, per the Texas Tribune; advocates see a path to a comprehensive regulated market when the session opens Jan 12, 2027. HB 46 TCUP expansion: 12 new dispensing licenses conditionally awarded (9 in Dec 2025, 3 in Apr 2026); licensees must be operational within 24 months
ib_angle: Build-out capital for new TCUP licensees; a new statewide leadership raises 2027 odds of widening the program toward a full regulated market, the largest remaining greenfield.
source: Marijuana Moment (Texas Tribune, Nov 5); Texas DPS

catalyst: State Supreme Court upheld the voter-approved medical law (Sep 4); first round of 4 product-manufacturing licenses (applications closed Jul 20) to be awarded by lottery
ib_angle: Greenfield medical market; early license holders become tuck-in targets.

catalyst: Adult-use retail licensing reopened Aug 7: up to 24 new retail licenses across six zones (6 social equity, 6 worker co-op, 12 general); applications close Nov 23 at 4 p.m. ET. On Oct 21 a federal judge dismissed the three residency suits as moot after the June law change
ib_angle: New doors in a small market next to MA and CT operators; the in-state majority-ownership rule is gone, opening the round to outside capital. No award timeline yet.
source: The Marijuana Herald; Rhode Island Current

catalyst: $1.1B annual market; TerrAscend paid $9M for a single store doing more than $10M a year
ib_angle: Scarce, high-volume doors in key counties support MSO tuck-ins.

catalyst: 87 retailers (~12% of licensees) on OCM's cash-on-delivery list owing ~$3.89M to 44 suppliers, ~281 days delinquent on average; OCM's largest illicit seizure (>$17M); S10643 (signed Oct 28, Ch. 369) ends the labor peace agreement mandate for licensees; its wage board and applicant ownership/pay disclosure rules take effect Jan 31, 2027 unless lawmakers pass promised amendments
ib_angle: Stressed single-store retailers → tuck-ins and distressed sales; dropping labor peace requirements lowers a compliance hurdle in license transfers and new builds.
source: Vicente LLP (COD list); NY Senate (S10643 signed Oct 28)

catalyst: First year of statewide adult-use retail (from Sep 16, 2025): >$250M combined sales (~$150M adult-use, ~$100M medical); 369 licensed businesses; 486,720 plants held by 102 license holders
ib_angle: Young adult-use market scaling quickly; supply build-out and licensee capital needs.

catalyst: Most active 2026 M&A state: Vireo (Schwazze, LivWell, Cannabist stores) and Spherex buying Cannabist grows; declining cultivation capacity
ib_angle: Mature, price-compressed market where scale buyers are consolidating at low per-door prices.

catalyst: Regulators approved Vireo–Planet 13 on Oct 15; Vireo closed C21 (Aug 21) and M3 Wellness (Sep 21). Interim revenue committee (Oct 27) reviewed scrapping the 15% wholesale tax for a 12–15% retail excise; no action, may return in the 2027 session
ib_angle: Consolidation of tourist-driven retail; remaining independents are natural targets. Removing the wholesale tax would favor cultivators' margins.
source: Marijuana Moment (Nevada Current, Oct 27); The Marijuana Herald (Vireo–Planet 13 approval)

catalyst: Democrats won control of the state House on Nov 3 (Republicans expected to keep the Senate); Gov. Stein supports a regulated adult-use market. Governor's advisory council issues regulatory recommendations in Dec 2026 as a 2027 roadmap; 63% back adult-use, 74% medical (SurveyUSA)
ib_angle: Large state with no regulated program; position ahead of 2027 bills.
source: The Marijuana Herald (Nov 4); Cannabis Business Times (council, poll)

catalyst: Gov. Green, who says he would sign a regulated adult-use bill, was reelected Nov 3 and Democrats kept large majorities in both chambers; only Democratic-trifecta state without adult-use
ib_angle: Legislative path is the clearest of the remaining holdouts.

catalyst: Democrat David Crowley, who backs full legalization, won the governor's race and Democrats flipped both chambers (Senate 18-15, Assembly 53 of 99) on Nov 3; legalization bills (AB 1061/SB 1045) could be revived in January; the incoming Assembly speaker and the Senate Democratic caucus chair said (Nov 5) the new majority will legalize. No medical program today
ib_angle: Surrounded by legal markets with no program; first unified Democratic control since 2010 gives a legislative path to a new market.

catalyst: Democrats won both chambers on Nov 3: about 292 of 400 House seats per the House Clerk, and a 15-9 Senate per the AP forecast, just shy of a veto-proof majority; results not final (recounts likely). Gov. Ayotte, who opposes legalization, was reelected
ib_angle: Legislature more receptive and the House may have a veto-proof margin, but the Senate looks one seat short, so a veto keeps near-term odds low; last New England holdout.

catalyst: Voters rejected HJR 4 on Nov 3 (66%+ no, unofficial), keeping the citizen-initiative path to legalization open; the 2026 medical initiative had failed to qualify
ib_angle: No program yet; initiative route stays open for a future medical measure.

catalyst: 24% wholesale excise since Jan 1, 2026 on top of the 10% retail excise and 6% sales tax; the industry challenge is back at the Court of Appeals on expedited review after an Apr 22 Supreme Court order, and a second suit alleges unconstitutional tax pyramiding
ib_angle: Margin compression is producing distressed sellers (adult-use sales down $50M year on year through March); a court win would remove the tax.

catalyst: Dispensary application window (Oct 26–30) for the six existing producers; the per-producer cap rises to nine stores after the patient registry passed 55,000 (56,650 patients as of Sep 23; 22 dispensing licenses as of Sep 30). A new delivery rule (Sep 30) also allows USPS shipment
ib_angle: Store build-out capital for the six license holders; no new cultivation licenses, so producer licenses stay scarce in a small, tightly licensed medical market. Delivery adds distribution reach.
source: Georgia Access to Medical Cannabis Commission (via The Marijuana Herald)

catalyst: Dispensary sales fell to about $1.5B in FY2026 from nearly $2B as prices drop, even with record unit volume (5M+ items in July); cannabis tax revenue $456M vs $474M; 29 new dispensary licenses issued this year
ib_angle: Price compression pressures smaller operators; limited-license structure still supports values.

catalyst: Local opt-outs still the rule nine years after legalization; Vireo–Eaze adds delivery scale
ib_angle: Fragmented, oversupplied market; delivery and distribution are the consolidation plays.
